cursor.meaning: the small arrow on the screen. It moves when you move the mouse.

click.meaning: press the left mouse button once, then let go.

doubleClick.meaning: press the left mouse button twice, quickly.

drag.meaning: hold the left mouse button down, move the mouse, then let go.

scroll.meaning: move the page up or down by turning the small wheel on the mouse.

backspace.meaning: the key that rubs out the letter just before the blinking line.

enter.meaning: the big key that starts a new line, or says “yes, go ahead”.

save.meaning: keep your work on the computer, so you can open it again later.

select.meaning: choose something so you can change it. It turns blue when chosen.

ribbon.meaning: the row of buttons along the top of Word.

file.meaning: one saved piece of work, like a letter or a photo.

browser.meaning: the program you use to open websites, such as Chrome.

home.title: Learn to use a computer, slowly and at your own pace.
home.intro: Digital Nati shows you one small step at a time — how to use the mouse, write a letter, send an email and stay safe on the internet. It is free, and there is no test to fail.
home.nameMeaning: “Nati” is Bangla for grandchild. Think of us as a patient grandchild sitting beside you.
home.marginNote: Take your time — there's no rush here.
home.how1Text: Each lesson starts with a video of 2 to 5 minutes. You can slow it down and watch it again as many times as you like.
home.how2Text: Practise on the screen, in a safe place. Nothing can break here, and a wrong click only gives you a hint.
home.how3Text: When you finish a course, print your certificate or keep it on the computer.
home.learnIntro: Start with the first course. Each one uses what you learned in the one before.
home.familiesText: Is your mother, father, grandmother or grandfather learning? You can set up their account, see how far they have come, and help them over WhatsApp — even if you live far away.
home.why1: Digital Nati is made by KARJO. Our founder faced real difficulties when he built a website for his own business. He turned that struggle into a simpler path, so others could skip it.
home.why2: That is how KARJO works. In Bangladesh, KARJO Prime helps businesses get online at a low price. Digital Nati does the same for people who never had the chance to learn computers.
home.why3: Nobody should have to struggle alone with a computer. Someone patient should sit beside them and show them, one step at a time.

helpPage.title: Help
helpPage.intro: You can call or WhatsApp us at any time, about anything. There is no silly question.
helpPage.q1: What if I click the wrong thing?
helpPage.a1: Nothing bad will happen. Most things can be undone. Look for a “Back” button or an arrow at the top left, or close the window and start again. On Digital Nati, a wrong click only gives you a hint.
helpPage.a2: No. Clicking, typing and trying things will not break it. Only two things need care: keep water away from it, and turn it off the proper way, from the Start menu.
helpPage.q3: Someone called saying they're from the bank, bKash or Nagad. What do I do?
helpPage.a3: Don't tell them any PIN, password or code that came by SMS. A real bank, bKash or Nagad will never ask you for these. Hang up, then call the number written on your card or in the official app yourself. If you're not sure, call us and we'll help you check.
helpPage.q4: I forgot what I learned yesterday. Is that normal?
helpPage.a4: Yes, completely normal. Everyone forgets at first. Watch the lesson again — it will always be here. You can also print the steps and keep them beside the computer.
helpPage.a5: No. Learning on Digital Nati is free.
helpPage.a6: Press the “Aa Text size” button at the top of the page and choose “Large” or “Extra large”.
helpPage.a7: On this computer. If you use a different computer, your ticks won't be there yet.

families.title: For families
families.intro: Helping a parent or grandparent learn the computer takes patience. Here is how Digital Nati can make it easier for both of you.
families.setup1: Open Digital Nati on the computer they will use.
families.setup3: Type their name and mobile number.
families.setup4: Tick “A family member is helping me” and add your own WhatsApp number.
families.setup5: Type the code, and you're done.
families.progressText: On their “My learning” page there is a button that sends you their progress on WhatsApp. Ask them to press it now and then, or press it yourself when you visit.
families.tip1: Let them hold the mouse. Don't take it from them, even when it is slow.
families.tip2: Explain one thing at a time. Stop after each step and let them try.
families.tip3: Write the steps on paper. The “Print this lesson” button on every lesson helps.
families.tip4: Never say “it's easy”. If it were easy, they would already know. Say “you're doing well”.
families.tip5: Laugh about mistakes together. Nothing can break.
families.tip6: Live far away? A WhatsApp video call, with your phone's camera pointed at their screen, works well.
families.contact: Questions? Call or WhatsApp us any time.
